speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand the severity and cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any specific triggers?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by choking, coughing, and severe chest pain, is classic for esophageal rupture. This is a surgical emergency; I will immediately order a CT scan with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
